name: The Sun
sections: Overview
The Sun is a middle-aged star at the centre of our Solar System. It holds 99.86% of the system’s total mass, and its gravity keeps everything from Mercury to the distant Oort Cloud in orbit.
How it shines

Deep in the core, nuclear fusion turns about 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium every second. The energy it releases takes up to 170,000 years to work its way out to the surface, then crosses to Earth in just over 8 minutes.
Structure

Energy moves outward through the radiative zone and then the convective zone, where huge bubbles of plasma rise and sink. The visible surface is the photosphere. Above it sit the chromosphere and the corona, which is strangely hotter than the surface at over a million °C.
Solar activity

The Sun runs on a roughly 11-year cycle of magnetic activity. At its peak, sunspots, solar flares and coronal mass ejections become common. They can disrupt satellites and power grids, and they create auroras on Earth.
Future
In about 5 billion years the Sun will run out of hydrogen in its core and swell into a red giant, possibly swallowing Mercury, Venus and maybe Earth. It will end as a slowly cooling white dwarf.
dyk: About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
The Parker Solar Probe has flown closer to the Sun than any other spacecraft, within about 6 million km of its surface.
The Sun is technically white. It only looks yellow through Earth’s atmosphere.

name: Proxima Centauri
tagline: The closest star to the Sun
sections: Overview
Proxima Centauri is a small, cool red dwarf. It belongs to the Alpha Centauri triple-star system, and it is the nearest known star to our Sun. It is too faint to see without a telescope.
Planets
Proxima b is a roughly Earth-mass planet orbiting in the star’s habitable zone, where liquid water could exist. It circles its star every 11.2 days.
A restless star
Proxima is a flare star. It sometimes brightens dramatically as its magnetic field releases energy. Those flares could strip atmospheres from nearby planets, which makes habitability uncertain.
dyk: Light from Proxima takes over 4 years to reach us.
At Voyager 1’s speed it would take over 70,000 years to get there.
Red dwarfs like Proxima can burn for trillions of years.

name: Sirius
tagline: The brightest star in the night sky
sections: Overview
Sirius looks so bright because it is both luminous and close by. It is actually a binary system. Sirius A is a hot white star, and Sirius B is a faint white dwarf companion.
History
The ancient Egyptians based their calendar on Sirius rising just before dawn, which signalled the annual flooding of the Nile. The phrase “dog days of summer” also comes from Sirius.
Sirius B
Sirius B was the first white dwarf ever discovered. It packs about the mass of the Sun into a ball roughly the size of Earth.
dyk: Only the Moon, Venus, Jupiter and sometimes Mars outshine Sirius.
Sirius is slowly getting closer to us.
A teaspoon of Sirius B would weigh several tonnes.

name: Betelgeuse
tagline: A red supergiant near its end
sections: Overview
Betelgeuse marks Orion’s shoulder. If it sat where the Sun is, its surface would reach beyond the orbit of Mars.
The Great Dimming
In late 2019 and early 2020 Betelgeuse dimmed to about 40% of its usual brightness. Astronomers found that the star had thrown off a huge cloud of dust, which briefly blocked its light.
Coming supernova

Betelgeuse is near the end of its life. At some point in the next 100,000 years it will explode as a supernova. For weeks it will be bright enough to see during the day, but it is too far away to harm Earth.
dyk: Betelgeuse is so young that dinosaurs were long extinct before it formed.
Its name comes from Arabic and is often translated as “hand of the giant”.
It is one of the few stars whose surface telescopes can resolve.

name: Neutron Stars
tagline: The densest stars in the universe
sections: Overview

When a massive star explodes, its core can collapse into a neutron star, an object about the size of a city but heavier than the Sun. Its matter is squeezed so tightly that protons and electrons merge into neutrons.
Pulsars
Many neutron stars spin rapidly and sweep beams of radiation across space like lighthouses. Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovered the first pulsar in 1967.
Kilonovae
When two neutron stars collide, they send out gravitational waves and forge heavy elements such as gold and platinum. The collision first detected in 2017 confirmed this.
dyk: A sugar-cube of neutron star weighs about a billion tonnes.
Magnetars are neutron stars with the strongest magnetic fields known.
The gold in your jewellery may have been made in a neutron star collision.

name: Mercury
sections: Overview
Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It races around its orbit faster than any other planet, which is why it was named after the Roman messenger god.
Surface
Its grey, heavily cratered surface looks like our Moon. With almost no atmosphere to trap heat, it swings from scorching days to freezing nights.
Interior
Mercury has a huge iron core that takes up about 85% of its radius. Its weak magnetic field suggests part of that core is still molten.
Exploration
Mariner 10 flew past it in 1974–75. MESSENGER orbited from 2011 to 2015 and found water ice in shadowed polar craters. The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is on its way.
dyk: Mercury is shrinking as its core cools, which wrinkles the surface.
From Mercury’s surface the Sun would look three times bigger than from Earth.
Despite being closest to the Sun, it is not the hottest planet. Venus is.

name: Venus
sections: Overview
Venus is almost the same size as Earth and is often called Earth’s twin. But it is a hellish world, with crushing pressure and temperatures hot enough to melt lead.
Atmosphere
A thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect. Clouds of sulfuric acid cover the planet and reflect sunlight, which makes Venus the brightest planet in our sky.
Strange spin
Venus rotates backwards compared to most planets, and so slowly that a day lasts longer than its year.
Exploration

The Soviet Venera landers sent back the first images from its surface before they failed in the heat. Radar from NASA’s Magellan mapped it in the 1990s. The DAVINCI and VERITAS missions are planned next.
dyk: On Venus the Sun rises in the west.
Its clouds circle the planet in just 4 days.
Venus has more volcanoes than any other planet.

name: Earth
tagline: The only known world with life
sections: Overview
Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only place we know of where life exists. It is the densest planet in the Solar System.
Atmosphere & water
A nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere and liquid oceans keep the climate stable. Plate tectonics recycles the crust and helps regulate carbon over millions of years.
Magnetic shield
Molten iron moving in the outer core creates a magnetic field. It deflects the solar wind and protects both the atmosphere and life on the surface.
Seen from space
Photos such as “Earthrise” (1968) and the “Pale Blue Dot” (1990) changed how people see the planet and helped inspire the environmental movement.
dyk: Earth is not a perfect sphere. It bulges at the equator.
Earth’s rotation is gradually slowing down.
Earth is the only planet not named after a god.

name: Mars
sections: Overview
Mars is a cold desert world. Iron-oxide dust gives it its rusty colour. It has seasons, polar ice caps and weather, including dust storms that can cover the whole planet.
Landmarks
Olympus Mons is the tallest volcano in the Solar System, about 22 km high. Valles Marineris is a canyon system about 4,000 km long.
Water & life
Dry riverbeds, deltas and minerals show that Mars once had liquid water. Rovers are searching ancient lakebeds for signs of past microbial life.
Exploration
More missions have been sent to Mars than to any other planet. Curiosity and Perseverance are exploring the surface today. Perseverance is collecting samples for a future return to Earth.
dyk: Mars has the largest dust storms in the Solar System.
Sunsets on Mars look blue.
Its two small moons are called Phobos and Deimos, meaning fear and panic.

name: Jupiter
sections: Overview
Jupiter is the largest planet. It is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined, and it is made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
Great Red Spot
This giant storm is wider than Earth and has raged for at least 350 years, although it has been shrinking.
Interior
Deep inside, the pressure turns hydrogen into a metal that conducts electricity. That creates the strongest magnetic field of any planet.
Exploration
Pioneer, Voyager, Galileo and now Juno have studied Jupiter. Juno revealed cyclones clustered at the poles and a “fuzzy” core. Europa Clipper and ESA’s JUICE are headed for its moons.
dyk: Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet.
It has faint rings, first spotted by Voyager 1.
Its gravity helps shield the inner planets from some comets.

name: Saturn
sections: Overview
Saturn is the second-largest planet and the least dense. Its spectacular ring system can be seen through even a small telescope.
The rings
The rings stretch up to 280,000 km across but are often only about 10 m thick. They are made of countless pieces of water ice, and they may be much younger than the planet.
Hexagon
A strange six-sided jet stream circles Saturn’s north pole. Each side is longer than Earth’s diameter.
Exploration
Cassini–Huygens orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017, dropped a probe onto Titan, and ended by diving into Saturn’s atmosphere.
dyk: Saturn has more known moons than any other planet.
Its rings are slowly raining down onto the planet.
Winds near its equator reach 1,800 km/h.

name: Uranus
sections: Overview
Uranus is an ice giant made mostly of water, methane and ammonia ices around a small rocky core. Methane gives it its pale cyan colour.
Tipped over
Uranus rotates on its side, probably because of a giant collision long ago. Each pole gets about 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.
Discovery
William Herschel discovered it in 1781. It was the first planet found with a telescope.
Exploration
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited, flying past in 1986. A dedicated orbiter is a top priority for future missions.
dyk: Uranus has the coldest atmosphere of any planet.
Its moons are named after characters from Shakespeare and Pope.
It has 13 known faint rings.

name: Neptune
sections: Overview
Neptune is the most distant planet from the Sun. It is a deep blue ice giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System.
Found by maths
In 1846 astronomers predicted where Neptune should be from wobbles in Uranus’s orbit, then found it almost exactly there.
Triton
Its largest moon orbits backwards and has geysers of nitrogen. Neptune may have captured it from the Kuiper Belt.
Exploration
Voyager 2 flew past in 1989 and spotted the Great Dark Spot, a storm the size of Earth that later vanished.
dyk: Neptune completed its first orbit since its discovery in 2011.
It radiates more heat than it gets from the Sun.
Sunlight takes about 4 hours to reach it.

name: Pluto
sections: Overview
Pluto is the largest known object in the Kuiper Belt. Clyde Tombaugh discovered it in 1930, and it counted as the ninth planet until 2006.
Why it was reclassified
The International Astronomical Union ruled that a planet must clear its orbital neighbourhood. Pluto shares its zone with many other icy bodies.
The heart
New Horizons flew past in 2015 and revealed Sputnik Planitia, a vast heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice. It also found water-ice mountains and a thin, blue, hazy atmosphere.
dyk: Pluto is smaller than Earth’s Moon.
Its moon Charon is so big that the two orbit a point in the space between them.
An 11-year-old girl, Venetia Burney, suggested the name Pluto.

name: The Moon
sections: Overview
The Moon is Earth’s only natural satellite and the fifth-largest moon in the Solar System. It steadies Earth’s tilt, which keeps our climate more stable.
Origin
The leading theory is that a Mars-sized body called Theia hit the young Earth, and the debris came together to form the Moon.
Tides & locking
The Moon’s gravity raises Earth’s ocean tides. It always shows us the same face because it is tidally locked.
Exploration
Apollo astronauts walked on it between 1969 and 1972. Missions from China, India and others have landed since. Through Artemis, NASA plans to send people back.
dyk: The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
Footprints on the Moon can last millions of years.
The far side is not dark. It gets just as much sunlight.

name: Io
sections: Overview
Io is the innermost of Jupiter’s four large moons. It is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System.
Why so active
Tidal flexing from Jupiter and the neighbouring moons Europa and Ganymede kneads Io’s interior and heats it enough to melt rock.
Surface
Lava lakes and sulfur deposits paint Io yellow, orange and red. Some volcanic plumes shoot 400 km into space.
dyk: Galileo discovered Io in 1610.
Its volcanoes resurface the whole moon constantly, so it has almost no craters.
Juno has flown close by and photographed erupting volcanoes.

name: Europa
sections: Overview
Europa is slightly smaller than our Moon. It is covered in a bright shell of ice criss-crossed with reddish cracks.
Hidden ocean
Beneath the ice is thought to lie a salty ocean holding about twice as much water as all of Earth’s oceans. Heat from tidal flexing keeps it liquid.
Life?
With water, chemical energy and the right ingredients, Europa is one of the best places to look for life beyond Earth.
Exploration
NASA’s Europa Clipper launched in 2024 and will make dozens of close flybys to study the ice and the ocean.
dyk: Hubble may have seen water plumes erupting from Europa.
Its surface is among the smoothest in the Solar System.
Radiation near Europa would be deadly to people within a day.

name: Ganymede
tagline: The largest moon in the Solar System
sections: Overview
Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury. It is the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field.
Subsurface ocean
Hubble watched Ganymede’s auroras wobble, which suggested a salty ocean deep beneath its icy crust.
Exploration
ESA’s JUICE mission launched in 2023 and will become the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than ours.
dyk: If it orbited the Sun, Ganymede would count as a planet.
It has faint auroras.
Its surface mixes dark ancient terrain with bright grooved regions.

name: Titan
sections: Overview
Titan is Saturn’s largest moon and the only moon with a thick atmosphere. It is also the only world besides Earth known to have stable liquid on its surface.
Weather
On Titan, methane plays the role that water plays on Earth. It forms clouds, falls as rain, carves rivers and fills lakes and seas near the poles.
Exploration
ESA’s Huygens probe landed there in 2005, the most distant landing ever. NASA’s Dragonfly helicopter is due to launch in 2028.
dyk: On Titan you could fly by flapping strapped-on wings.
Its atmosphere is mostly nitrogen, like Earth’s.
Titan is larger than the planet Mercury.

name: Enceladus
sections: Overview
Enceladus is a small, bright icy moon. It reflects almost all the sunlight that hits it, which makes it one of the whitest objects in the Solar System.
Geysers
Cassini found jets of water vapour and ice shooting from “tiger stripe” fractures near its south pole. They feed Saturn’s E ring.
Habitability
Cassini flew through the plumes and detected salts, organic molecules and signs of hydrothermal activity, which are key ingredients for life.
dyk: Enceladus would fit inside the UK.
It is one of the top targets in the search for life.
Its plumes reach hundreds of km above the surface.

name: Comets
sections: Overview
Comets are leftover building blocks from the birth of the Solar System. They are frozen mixtures of ice, dust and rock.
Tails
Near the Sun, the ice turns straight to gas, forming a glowing coma and two tails. The dust tail curves, and the ion tail points directly away from the Sun.
Exploration
ESA’s Rosetta orbited comet 67P and landed the Philae probe on it in 2014. NASA’s Deep Impact fired a projectile into comet Tempel 1.
dyk: Comet tails always point away from the Sun.
Comets may have delivered some of Earth’s water.
Halley’s Comet shows up about every 76 years.

name: Asteroid Belt
tagline: Rocky leftovers between Mars and Jupiter
sections: Overview
The main asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter. Jupiter’s gravity stopped these rocks from ever forming a planet.
Not crowded
Despite the millions of asteroids, the belt is mostly empty space. Spacecraft fly through it without dodging anything.
Planetary defence
In 2022 NASA’s DART spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos and successfully changed its orbit. It was the first test of deflecting an asteroid.
dyk: Ceres is a dwarf planet and may hold salty water.
The Psyche mission is visiting a metal-rich asteroid.
Samples from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu have been brought back to Earth.

name: Meteor Showers
sections: Overview
Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through trails of dust left behind by comets. The particles burn up in the atmosphere as streaks of light.
Terms
In space it is a meteoroid. As it glows through the air it is a meteor. If a piece reaches the ground, it is a meteorite.
Watching
Go somewhere dark, let your eyes adjust for 20 minutes and look at a wide patch of sky. The best hours are usually after midnight.
dyk: Most meteors are smaller than a grain of sand.
The Geminids come from an asteroid, 3200 Phaethon.
Tonnes of space dust fall on Earth every day.

name: Milky Way
sections: Overview
The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy. The Sun sits about 26,000 light-years from its centre, in a minor spiral arm called the Orion Spur.
Centre
At the core sits Sagittarius A*, a black hole about 4 million times the mass of the Sun. The Event Horizon Telescope imaged it in 2022.
Neighbourhood
The Milky Way belongs to the Local Group of more than 80 galaxies, and it is slowly absorbing several smaller dwarf galaxies.
dyk: On dark nights you see the Milky Way as a band of light, which is the galaxy’s disk seen from inside.
The galaxy is surrounded by an invisible halo of dark matter.
The Gaia spacecraft has mapped nearly 2 billion of its stars.

name: Andromeda
sections: Overview
Andromeda is the largest galaxy in the Local Group and the most distant object visible to the naked eye.
Proof of other galaxies
In the 1920s Edwin Hubble measured the distance to Andromeda. That showed it lies far outside the Milky Way and proved the universe contains other galaxies.
Collision course
Andromeda is approaching at about 110 km/s. In billions of years the two galaxies will merge into one giant elliptical galaxy, sometimes nicknamed “Milkomeda”.
dyk: Andromeda looks six times wider than the full Moon in the sky, but it is very faint.
The light you see from it left 2.5 million years ago.
Stars almost never collide during galaxy mergers.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
sections: Overview
We see the Sombrero almost edge-on. A bright central bulge and a dark ring of dust make it look like a wide-brimmed hat.
Webb’s view
In infrared light, Webb shows the dust ring as clumpy and detailed. The bright bulge fades away, turning the galaxy into a glowing target.
dyk: It is visible through small backyard telescopes.
Its central black hole is among the heaviest in nearby galaxies.
It hosts around 2,000 globular clusters.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
sections: Overview
The Whirlpool is famous for its two well-defined spiral arms, which are dotted with pink star-forming regions.
Interaction
A smaller companion galaxy, NGC 5195, is tugging on one arm. That interaction probably sharpens the spiral pattern and triggers new stars.
History
In 1845 Lord Rosse sketched its spiral structure. It was the first galaxy recognised as having one.
dyk: Charles Messier discovered it in 1773.
Several supernovae have been seen in it recently.
Hubble’s image of M51 is one of its most famous.

name: Orion Nebula
sections: Overview
The Orion Nebula is the closest large star-forming region to Earth. You can see it as a fuzzy patch in Orion’s sword.
Star birth
Thousands of young stars are forming inside it. Many are surrounded by protoplanetary disks, called proplyds, where planets may form.
The Trapezium
Four hot, massive stars at its heart light up the surrounding gas and carve out a cavity in it.
dyk: It is one of the most photographed objects in the sky.
Webb found strange Jupiter-mass objects drifting freely inside it.
It is part of a much larger cloud complex in Orion.

name: Crab Nebula
sections: Overview
The Crab Nebula is the expanding debris of a star that exploded as a supernova. Chinese astronomers recorded the explosion in 1054 AD.
The pulsar
A neutron star spinning 30 times a second powers the nebula and makes it glow across the whole spectrum, from radio waves to gamma rays.
Still growing
The nebula is expanding at about 1,500 km/s.
dyk: The 1054 supernova was visible in daylight for 23 days.
It was the first object in Charles Messier’s catalogue.
Its tangled filaments are rich in elements forged in the star.

name: Pillars of Creation
sections: Overview
The Pillars of Creation are towering columns of cold gas and dust inside the Eagle Nebula, where new stars are being born.
Being eroded
Intense light from nearby massive stars is slowly boiling the pillars away, a process called photoevaporation.
Webb’s view
Webb’s infrared image in 2022 cut through the dust to show newborn stars glowing like red lava at the tips of the pillars.
dyk: The tallest pillar is about 4 light-years long.
Hubble’s 1995 photo is among the most famous space images ever.
Stars inside are only a few hundred thousand years old.

name: Ring Nebula
sections: Overview
The Ring Nebula is a planetary nebula, the glowing shell of gas thrown off by a Sun-like star near the end of its life.
Not planets
The name “planetary nebula” comes from early telescopes, where these objects looked round like planets. They have nothing to do with planets.
A preview
Our Sun will probably make a similar nebula in about 5 billion years.
dyk: The ring is actually shaped more like a donut or barrel.
Webb revealed about 20,000 dense clumps of gas in it.
It is easy to find with a backyard telescope.

name: Black Holes
sections: Overview
A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses the boundary called the event horizon.
How they form
Stellar black holes form when very massive stars collapse. Supermassive black holes, millions to billions of times the Sun’s mass, sit at the centres of most galaxies.
Seeing the invisible
Black holes are spotted through their effects: glowing disks of gas, stars whipping around them, and gravitational waves from mergers, first detected by LIGO in 2015.
dyk: Near a black hole, time runs slower.
Stephen Hawking predicted that black holes slowly evaporate.
Our galaxy’s central black hole is about 26,000 light-years away.

name: Supernovae
sections: Overview
A supernova is the explosive death of a star. For a few weeks it can outshine an entire galaxy.
Two main kinds
Massive stars explode when their cores collapse. A white dwarf can explode when it takes on too much matter from a companion star (Type Ia).
Star stuff
Supernovae scatter elements like oxygen, calcium and iron across space. Those elements end up in new stars, planets and people.
dyk: Type Ia supernovae helped reveal that the universe’s expansion is speeding up.
Supernova 1987A was the closest seen in modern times.
The iron in your blood came from exploding stars.

name: Aurora
sections: Overview
Auroras are curtains of light that form when charged particles from the Sun collide with gases in Earth’s upper atmosphere.
Where & when
They usually appear in rings around the magnetic poles. During strong solar storms they can be seen much farther from the poles.
Other worlds
Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune all have auroras, and so do moons such as Ganymede.
dyk: The Northern Lights are called aurora borealis and the Southern Lights aurora australis.
Astronauts on the ISS often fly over auroras.
The strong solar storm of May 2024 brought auroras unusually far from the poles.

name: Solar Eclipses
tagline: When the Moon blocks the Sun
sections: Overview
A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and casts its shadow on Earth.
A cosmic coincidence
The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon but also about 400 times farther away, so they look almost the same size in our sky.
Safety
Never look at the Sun without certified eclipse glasses. It is only safe to look with the naked eye during the brief moment of totality.
dyk: During totality you can see the Sun’s corona.
Helium was discovered in the Sun’s light during an eclipse in 1868.
Millions of years from now, total eclipses will no longer happen.

name: The Big Bang
sections: Overview
The Big Bang is the scientific theory that the universe started in an extremely hot, dense state about 13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.
Not an explosion
It was not an explosion in space. Space itself began expanding everywhere at once.
Evidence
Galaxies moving away from us, the leftover cosmic microwave background, and the amounts of hydrogen and helium in the universe all support the theory.
dyk: The term “Big Bang” was coined as a joke.
Some of the static on old analogue TVs came from the Big Bang’s afterglow.
Webb is seeing galaxies from just a few hundred million years after it.

name: Dark Matter
sections: Overview
Dark matter is an invisible substance that does not give off, absorb or reflect light. We only detect it through its gravity.
Evidence
Galaxies spin too fast to hold together with visible matter alone. Galaxy clusters also bend light more strongly than their visible mass can explain.
The search
Scientists are hunting for dark-matter particles with underground detectors, particle colliders and space telescopes such as ESA’s Euclid.
dyk: Vera Rubin’s galaxy rotation studies were key evidence.
Dark matter may be passing through you right now.
Without it, galaxies might never have formed.

name: Dark Energy
sections: Overview
In 1998 astronomers found that the universe’s expansion is speeding up, not slowing down. The unknown cause is called dark energy.
What could it be?
One idea is that it is energy belonging to empty space itself, Einstein’s “cosmological constant.” Recent surveys hint that it may change over time.
Fate of the universe
If dark energy keeps pushing, distant galaxies will eventually disappear beyond our view.
dyk: Dark energy makes up most of the universe.
The expansion began speeding up about 5 billion years ago.
Nobody knows what it really is.

name: Exoplanets
sections: Overview
Exoplanets are planets that orbit stars other than the Sun. Most stars probably have at least one.
How we find them
Telescopes watch for tiny dips in starlight as a planet passes in front of its star, or measure a star’s wobble as a planet tugs on it.
Searching for life
Webb can analyse the atmospheres of some exoplanets, looking for water, carbon dioxide and possible signs of life.
dyk: Some exoplanets orbit two suns, like Tatooine.
TRAPPIST-1 has seven Earth-sized planets.
Some “hot Jupiters” circle their star in less than a day.

name: Cosmic Microwave Background
tagline: The oldest light in the universe
sections: Overview
The cosmic microwave background (CMB) is faint radiation that fills the whole sky. It is the afterglow of the Big Bang.
Discovery
Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson found it by accident in 1965 while trying to get rid of static in a radio antenna.
A baby picture
Tiny temperature ripples in the CMB are the seeds that later grew into galaxies. Planck mapped them in fine detail.
dyk: At first it was mistaken for noise from pigeon droppings in the antenna.
It is the same in every direction to within 0.001%.
It is the best evidence for the Big Bang.

name: Space Station
sections: Overview
The International Space Station is a joint project of the US, Russia, Europe, Japan and Canada. People have lived on board continuously since November 2000.
Science
Its crews study how microgravity affects the human body, materials, plants and fluids, which helps prepare for longer missions.
Future
The ISS is planned to retire around 2030, when SpaceX will steer it down into the ocean. Commercial space stations are being built to replace it.
dyk: You can see the ISS from Earth without a telescope.
Astronauts on board see about 16 sunrises every day.
It is about the size of a football field.

name: Hubble Telescope
sections: Overview
The Hubble Space Telescope orbits above Earth’s blurring atmosphere and has captured some of the most famous images in astronomy.
A rocky start
Its main mirror had a tiny flaw. In 1993 astronauts installed corrective optics, and five Space Shuttle servicing missions have kept it working.
Discoveries
Hubble helped pin down the age of the universe, showed that nearly every galaxy has a supermassive black hole, and helped discover dark energy.
dyk: Hubble is named after astronomer Edwin Hubble.
It travels at about 27,000 km/h.
Its Deep Field images revealed thousands of galaxies in a tiny patch of sky.

name: James Webb Telescope
sections: Overview
Webb is the most powerful space telescope ever built. It observes infrared light to see through dust and back to the early universe.
Engineering
Its gold-coated beryllium mirror and five-layer sunshield had to unfold in space. The sunshield keeps the instruments at about −233 °C.
Discoveries
Webb has found surprisingly bright early galaxies, detected carbon dioxide on exoplanets, and made stunning images of nebulae and planets.
dyk: Webb’s mirror is about 6 times larger in area than Hubble’s.
It orbits a point in space, not Earth.
Its first full-colour image was released in July 2022.

name: Voyager 1
sections: Overview
Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn, then carried on outward. In 2012 it became the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space.
Pale Blue Dot
In 1990 it turned around and photographed Earth from 6 billion km away as a tiny speck, which Carl Sagan made famous.
Golden Record
On board is a gold-plated record with sounds, music and images from Earth, a message for anyone who might find it.
dyk: It runs on a power source that generates less energy each year.
Its computers have about 70 KB of memory.
Voyager 2 is the only probe to visit Uranus and Neptune.

name: Apollo 11
sections: Overview
Apollo 11 was the first mission to land humans on the Moon, fulfilling President Kennedy’s 1961 goal.
The landing
Neil Armstrong steered the lunar module Eagle past a boulder field and landed with only about 25 seconds of landing fuel left.
Legacy
About 600 million people watched live. Six Apollo missions landed in total, and 12 astronauts walked on the Moon.
dyk: Its guidance computer was far less powerful than a modern calculator.
Astronauts left a reflector that is still used to measure the Moon’s distance.
Michael Collins orbited alone while the others walked on the surface.

name: Perseverance Rover
tagline: Hunting for ancient life on Mars
sections: Overview
Perseverance is NASA’s most advanced Mars rover. It is exploring Jezero Crater, a lake bed that was once filled with water.
Samples
The rover collects rock cores in sealed tubes so that a future mission can bring them back to Earth for study.
Ingenuity
Its companion helicopter Ingenuity made the first powered flight on another world and went on to complete 72 flights.
dyk: It carries microphones and has recorded sounds on Mars.
Its MOXIE experiment made oxygen from Mars’s air.
It carries a chip with 10.9 million names from the public.

name: Artemis Program
tagline: Back to the Moon, to stay
sections: Overview
Artemis is NASA’s program to return humans to the Moon and build a lasting presence there, as a step towards Mars.
Missions
Artemis I tested the SLS rocket and the Orion capsule around the Moon in 2022. Artemis II sends astronauts around the Moon, and Artemis III aims to land near the south pole.
Gateway
A small lunar-orbit station called Gateway is planned as a hub for crews and science.
dyk: In Greek myth, Artemis is Apollo’s twin sister.
Artemis plans to land the first woman on the Moon.
The south pole may hold water ice in shadowed craters.
